name: Arrow
entries: Arrows are used with a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.
Arrows are typically stored in a {@item Quiver|XPHB} (bought separately).

name: Glaur
entries: Short, curved horns like a cornucopia. Played with valves, glaur sound like trumpets, while those without valves, known as gloon, have a more mournful sound.

name: Hand Drum
entries: A double-headed skin drum fitted with handles along its side.

name: Hooked Shortspear
entries: On a hit with this weapon, the wielder can forgo dealing damage and attempt to trip the target, in which case the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall {@condition prone}. The DC is 8 + the wielder's Strength modifier + the wielder's proficiency bonus.

name: Hoopak
entries: A hoopak is a sturdy stick with a sling at one end and a pointed tip at the other.

entries.name: Special

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a net is {@condition restrained} until it is freed. A net has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a {@dc 10} Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it, ending the effect and destroying the net. When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a net, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries: A recorder, a simple type of flute, usually carved from wood.

name: Spiked Armor
entries: Spiked armor is a rare type of medium armor made by dwarves. It consists of a leather coat and leggings covered with spikes that are usually made of metal.

name: Tantan
entries: A tambourine, a popular instrument with halflings and humans south of the Dalelands.

name: Thelarr
entries: Also known as a whistlecane, a simple and easy-to-make wind instrument cut from a reed. They are so simple, in fact, that skilled bards frequently make and give them away to children—to the parents' delight or regret.

name: Yarting
entries: A southern instrument from Amn and Calimshan that is a Faerûnian analog to the guitar. Numerous variations have spread across the continent.

name: Yklwa
entries: A yklwa (pronounced YICK-ul-wah) is a simple melee weapon that is the traditional weapon of Chultan warriors. A yklwa consists of a 3-foot wooden shaft with a steel or stone blade up to 18 inches long. Although it has the thrown weapon property, the yklwa is not well balanced for throwing.

name: Zulkoon
entries: A complex pump organ that originated with the zulkirs of Thay, who use it in the casting of their spells. It is considered to have a dramatic, but sinister, sound.

name: +1 Acid Fighting Chain
entries: {@note This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.}

Instead, the chains can be used to make a magic chain weapon {@homebrew |(see Grim Hollow Player's Guide)}. Such a weapon offers a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, and when the wielder hits with an attack using such a weapon, it deals {@damage 1d6} extra Acid damage. Each of these rare items requires 10 days and additional materials worth 1,000 GP to make.

name: Assault Rifle
entries: Combining a high rate of fire with rifle-grade ballistics, the Assault Rifle is a staple weapon for all modern militaries. Dozens of variants exist on this general design, but all share the traits of a flexible and formidable weapon.

name: Blunderbuss
entries: This distinctive short-range firearm features a dramatically flared muzzle designed to launch shot in a wide spray. Most effective at close range, the Blunderbuss can be considered a precursor to the modern shotgun.

name: Bullet
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Cannon
entries: Smoothbore, muzzleloading Cannons are common fixtures on pirate ships and defensive fortifications, capable of splintering wood and reducing stone to gravel with a thunderous boom. Larger siege weapons of this type exist, and require entire teams of operators to position, load, and fire.

name: Cannonball
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Double-Barrel Shotgun
entries: A classic design with two loaded barrels, the Double-Barrel Shotgun trades ammo capacity and range for reliability and firepower.

name: Flare
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Flare Gun
entries: Less a firearm and more a survival tool, a Flare Gun fires a single white-hot flare, useful for distress signals and last-ditch-effort self defense.

name: Gatling Gun
entries: Infamous for its rate of fire, the Gatling Gun rotates and fires six or more barrels in succession. This weapon is cumbersome, easily recognizable, and utterly terrifying.

name: Handgun
entries: Portable, reliable, and with a generous magazine size, the Handgun is the go-to firearm for self-defense and law enforcement.

name: Hunting Rifle
entries: Designed for big game, Hunting Rifles are slow but accurate, requiring bolt action operation between every shot.

name: Magnum
entries: Chambered for large-caliber bullets, Magnum revolvers pack the most kick possible into a single shot.

name: Parlor Gun
entries: The smallest usable firearm, a Parlor Gun can be tucked into a stocking or hidden down a sleeve for two barrels of point-blank fire.

name: Pistol
entries: The earliest type of one-handed firearm, a Pistol operates as a miniature Musket, loading and firing a single heavy projectile with deadly results.

name: Pump Shotgun
entries: The Pump Shotgun's namesake is a distinctive sliding grip on the barrel which can be "pumped" to chamber a new round.

name: Revolver
entries: An iconic handgun, the Revolver stores six bullets in a rotating cylinder. This weapon is favored by Gunslingers for its reliability and stopping-power.

name: Shell
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Shot
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Sniper Rifle
entries: An instrument of ranged precision, the Sniper Rifle can take shots from distant, nearly invisible ranges.

name: Submachine Gun
entries: Firing lighter, easier to control rounds, the Submachine Gun is an effective alternative to larger automatic weapons.

entries.name: Special
entries: As an action, a bayonet can be mounted to any two-handed ranged weapon or removed from it. While mounted, you can use the bayonet to make a two-handed melee weapon attack, which deals 1d8 piercing damage on a hit.

entries.name: Special
entries: A creature hit by a bolas falls {@condition prone} until it is freed. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bolas (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it, ending the effect and destroying the bolas. You can only throw one bolas on your turn.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is used to immobilize creatures at a distance. When you hit a creature of Large size or smaller with this weapon, you can attempt to {@action grapple} the creature instead of dealing damage. This {@action grapple} check uses your attack roll instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

entries.name: Special
entries: You can use an action to tie a rope to the end of a harpoon before it is thrown. If a rope-tied harpoon hits a target, it becomes embedded in the target, and you can use an action on subsequent turns to hold fast to the rope and make an opposed Strength (Athletics) check against the target to pull it up to 10 feet closer to you. Additionally, when the target moves, you can use your reaction to make an opposed Strength (Athletics) check against it, preventing its movement on a success. If you use your action to do anything else, you lose your grip on the rope. If the target has hands, it can remove the harpoon as an action.

entries.name: Special
entries: This is a one-handed weapon, usable only if you are missing a hand or have a special cuff designed to fit over your hand. Any humanoid that is missing a hand and regularly wears a hook has proficiency with this weapon.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures. This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures. Reloading this weapon requires 2 actions.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures. Reloading this weapon requires 2 actions.

name: Antimatter Carbine
entries: A more lethal model of the {@item Standard Carbine|ValdaSpire24Extras}, this rifle can automatically fire bolts of antimatter with surprising accuracy.

name: Antimatter Pistol
entries: A compact, antimatter-firing companion to the {@item Antimatter Carbine|ValdaSpire24Extras}, the {@item Antimatter Pistol|ValdaSpire24Extras} is an essential close-quarters backup.

name: Avia-Ra Sunstaff
entries: This long staff, forked at its end near a prominent gemstone, is a blaster in its own right. When used in expert hands, the Sunstaff can bludgeon, trip, and strike foes as a {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, only to be squeezed in both hands to fire a burst of hot plasma.

name: Blitz Cannon
entries: With its imposing rectangular muzzle, this brutalist weapon has a clear right and wrong end. Pulling its trigger unleashes a torrent of lightning bolts in a wide, imprecise spray, making it extremely dangerous at point-blank range.

name: Bolt Caster
entries: An early but reliable blaster design that resembles a crossbow, the Bolt Caster issues single shots of plasma with a long cooldown between shots.

entries.name: Missed Bombs
entries: For simplicity, we assume that a missed attack roll using a Bomb explodes harmlessly in the background or fails to detonate altogether. The GM decides the secondary effects of a miss, if any.

name: Concussion Rifle
entries: A series of arcane capacitors run the length of this rifle, terminating in a thick condenser that compresses its blast into a precise burst. A Concussion Rifle is especially deadly at long ranges, and its damage bypasses most energetically-resistant armor.

name: Dueling Laser
entries: A pistol intended for honorable, one-on-one duels, the Dueling Laser fires a blinding streak of light and promptly overheats. Spacers favor a Dueling Laser in their offhand for an infrequent but powerful retort.

name: Grenade
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Ion Cannon
entries: The Ion Cannon fires a bright, diffuse cone, rendering it deadly up close. Between shots, it makes a quiet zipping noise, as the arcane battery charges the ion cell for another blast.

name: Magnus
entries: This impressive handgun weighs almost twice that of a Repeater. Its infamous heft, recoil, and stopping power make it a favorite of spacers that accept no compromises.

name: Phaser
entries: Phasers aren't designed for effectiveness so much as portability and non-lethality. These blasters are often issued to peace-keepers and emissaries that require personal defense but have no intent to kill.

name: Plasma Launcher
entries: This short tube launches an orb of superheated plasma in an arc. On contact, the ball of plasma pops like a balloon, exploding in a dazzling fireball of sparks.

name: REC Gun
entries: The Revolving Exothermic Cannon (or REC gun, for short) operates on the same principle as a conventional blaster, with an arcane battery hooked up to an aperture barrel and so forth, but mounts several blasters on a revolving cylinder and fires each in rapid succession. A tripod mount keeps the blaster stable despite its heft and shocking recoil.

name: Repeater
entries: The quintessential handheld blaster, the Repeater is a staple on the Galactic Frontier. Solid, reliable, and packing just enough firepower to bring down an assailant, nearly every explorer worth their salt has one of these blasters strapped to their hip.

name: Standard Carbine
entries: As its name might suggest, the Standard Carbine is the standard-issue blaster for all Hegemony and Coalition troops, which makes it one of the most pervasive weapons in the 'Verse. Spacers of all stripes employ it for its compact size and superb accuracy.

name: Swarm Pistol
entries: This handheld blaster, styled much like a {@item Repeater|ValdaSpire24Extras}, has a wickedly fast automatic fire, capable of spewing dozens of rays in seconds. Dexterous users might even find it possible to use one in each hand for a dazzling spectacle of plasma bolts.
